7.0.0.en: In the first chapters of this book Jeremiah speaks in the midst of the people so that they repent, but now he stands publicly in the most important place, the gate of the house of the LORD, that is, His holy temple in Jerusalem, where those who come to worship God and bow down to Him throng, to rebuke everyone, people and leaders and priests, in the chapters (chs. 7-10), that perhaps they will repent. This of course brought him many problems, since the leaders rose up against him and tried to kill him several times.

7.1.0.en: God declares Himself with the attribute of power, that is, the LORD of hosts, and commands His people to amend their works, that is, to repent of their evil works, so that He forgives them and allows them to remain in the holy land, that is, the land of Canaan; and the opposite is true: if they do not repent He will drive them out of it, and this is what happened at the hands of the Babylonians.

7.2.0.en: God promised His people that He would keep His house forever if they lived with Him by faith, as in the days of King Hezekiah when Sennacherib attacked him, or when they built the temple in the days of Solomon (Isa 33:20; 1 Kgs 9:3). This was on condition of their steadfastness in faith, but they did not understand this and thought that the temple would not be demolished and that their city Jerusalem would remain firm however great their evil.

7.2.1.en: And God fulfilled His word in the permanence of His temple in the New Testament, to which the temple of the Old Testament points as a symbol, and this temple remains firm forever in the Kingdom of Heaven, where Christ reigns with those who believe in Him.

7.3.0.en: God requires of His people, so that He may keep them in the holy land, the land of promise, that they do the following:

7.3.1.en: 1- Hold fast to justice in dealings.

7.3.2.en: 2- Not oppress the weak, such as the stranger, the orphan and the widow.

7.3.3.en: 3- Not kill the innocent to fulfil their greed and gains.

7.3.4.en: 4- Keep away from the worship of idols.

7.3.5.en: It was in God's plan from eternity to give His people the Promised Land, and His promise remains for His people who believe in Him, who will receive faith in Christ, and He gives them the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, which lasts forever.

7.3.6.en: However great your opportunity for material gain, do not wrong another even if the law does not punish you, for God sees your works and punishes you for them if you do not repent. And know that He has mercy on the one who has mercy on others, so give up material things to gain what is more important, which is your eternal life, even if you give up some of your rights.

7.4.0.en: God rebukes His people because of their reliance on the words of the false prophets who promised them peace and security in spite of their evils, so they persisted in them.

7.5.0.en: God also rebukes His people for treating many sins as permissible, such as stealing, murder, adultery, swearing falsely and the worship of idols, and refusing to repent of them, and then drawing near to God and worshiping Him, thinking that this outward worship is enough for their salvation.

7.6.0.en: By their insistence on evil and their entering to offer worship to God, they make His house a den of robbers, because they steal the rights of others and come forward to worship God, so God does not accept their worship, but they defile the house of God by their entering it, and make it a meeting place for the wicked who insist on their evil. God is long-suffering and sees all this evil, but He will punish them if they do not repent.

7.7.0.en: Shiloh: a city located north of Bethel, 17 miles north of Jerusalem, in which the Ark of the Covenant of God was placed for about 300 years in the days of Joshua the son of Nun and in the time of the judges, until it went out to war with the sons of Eli the priest against the Philistines, who took it from them. It did not return to Shiloh, which was ruined afterwards, and it had been destroyed in the time of Jeremiah.

7.7.1.en: The people thought that Jerusalem would not be destroyed because of the presence of the temple of God in it, so He reminds them of the city of Shiloh, in which the Tabernacle of Meeting was and which was destroyed because of the evil of those who dwelt in it, so that they might repent of their sins.

7.8.0.en: The people rejected the word of God through His prophets, whether the early ones, that is, those who prophesied before the Assyrian captivity or during it, or before the Babylonian captivity, such as Jeremiah, so God warns them because of their disobedience.

7.9.0.en: God warns them that He will allow the destruction of His temple and Jerusalem His city and all the kingdom of Judah, as He allowed the Assyrian captivity that struck Shiloh, where the place of His Ark of the Covenant was, and indeed all the land of Ephraim, by which all the kingdom of Israel is meant, that is, the northern kingdom whose capital was Samaria, because of their evils.

7.10.0.en: God speaks to Jeremiah and forbids him to pray for this people who persist in their evils, for the prayers of Jeremiah and his importunity in asking for them will not profit them. Here He affirms the uselessness of a relationship with the Church, or of the prayers of the saints, as long as we insist on evil.

7.10.1.en: Do not rely on your outward relationship with the Church, or on your position and name in it, if you were a servant in it or gave something to it, if you insist on your sins. God calls you to return to Him, and then all your worship and works become acceptable and good in His eyes, and you benefit from the prayers of the saints and their intercession.

7.11.0.en: It seems that the feelings of the prophet Jeremiah were affected when God forbade him to pray for the people, so God makes clear to him here the appalling nature of what the people do, and calls him to see what is happening, which is the cooperation of the whole family to offer worship to idols. The sons, full of vitality, gather wood from different places, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead the dough to make cakes for the pagan gods, from whom they choose the queen of heaven. Thus we find the whole family, that is, the whole society, plunged into the worship of idols.

7.11.1.en: May every family encourage one another to live with God, whether in prayers, or in group readings at home, or in attachment to the Church and its activities, and if possible may they encourage one another in service and in works of mercy, so that it truly becomes a spiritual family.

7.12.0.en: The people plunged into the worship of idols and by this they fell into two things:

7.12.2.en: 2- They were filled with shame by their worship of stones and wood, that is, the worship of idols.

7.13.0.en: Because of the plunging into the worship of idols, and the refusal to repent and return to God, He had to punish not only the people for their evil, but all the creation that He created for them, so that they take notice when they lose their material comfort and repent.

7.14.0.en: God Almighty, the LORD of hosts, declares His rejection of the sacrifices that the children of Israel offer to Him, so He does not bless them or sanctify them, but regards them as mere ordinary slaughtered meat, and says to those who offer them, eat them as meat, for I reject them as burnt offerings because of your worship of idols and your persisting in sins.

7.15.0.en: God makes clear that when He called His people to bring them out of the land of Egypt, He did not intend that they should slaughter mere sacrifices to eat their meat, but He commanded them to slaughter the Passover lamb, which signifies Christ, that they might be saved by it from the destroying angel; He asks for the spiritual meaning and purity of heart, which are signified by the sacrifice and the burnt offering.

7.16.0.en: God declares His purpose and His requirements of His people, which are that they believe in Him, obey His word and walk with Him, and so receive blessing and kindness from God, and become His own people whom He cares for.

7.17.0.en: They turned their back: they rejected the word of God.

7.17.1.en: The people rejected the word of God and did not live by it, but walked according to their hearts, which were full of evil.

7.18.0.en: They hardened their neck: as the animal stiffens its neck so that the wooden yoke is not put on it to pull the agricultural implement, so the necks of His people became stiff, refusing to submit to God. God sent His prophets long ago, “early,” and sent His word with them, but the people rejected it and remained in their sins. He means the prophets from their going out of Egypt, that is, the prophet Moses, until Jeremiah.

7.19.0.en: In spite of the people's stubbornness and persistence in sin, God commanded Jeremiah to speak to them the word of God, and so that he would not be distressed He told him that they would reject him, and then Jeremiah proclaims to them that they are the people who reject the word of God and His discipline, so they departed from the truth in their speech and conduct.

7.19.1.en: Do not neglect the voice of God that you hear, not only in the Church and from your father of confession, but also what you hear from those around you, lest God condemn you because of your error.

7.20.s.en: (5) Rejected His house and His people

7.20.0.en: Cut off thine hair: hair is the crown of a woman, and in the case of intense grief she cuts it and shears it as the wool of sheep is sheared, and throws it on the ground, that is, she loses her beauty.

7.20.1.en: Lamentation: sad words by which the soul expresses its hard calamity, in a last attempt by God to save the kingdom of Judah; He addresses her as a woman and asks her to cut off her hair and raise a lamentation over the people of God whom He has rejected in “His wrath,” that is, over herself.

7.21.0.en: Their abominations: statues of the pagan gods that God hates.

7.21.1.en: The people defied God and placed in His holy temple the statues of the pagan gods whom they worship, so in their eyes God became merely one of the gods, equal to the idols in their worship of Him.

7.21.2.en: How hard is what you do when your heart is occupied, beside the worship of God, with money and various lusts, which even become your first concern that takes up most of your time, and you are troubled when they diminish. By this you make many idols within your heart, and forget God who gave you His whole life on the Cross, and who asks you to love Him with all your heart and to use the world in such a way that it does not rule your heart.

7.22.0.en: Tophet: its meaning is place of fire, and it is high places beside the valley of Hinnom on which they offered burnt offerings to the pagan gods.

7.22.1.en: The valley of the son of Hinnom: a valley south of Jerusalem into which the remains of sacrifices are thrown and burned with fire, and therefore the fire is always burning in it, and from it the name Gehenna was taken, that is, eternal torment and continual fire. To burn their sons and their daughters: they used to offer their children as burnt offerings to the pagan god “Molech” so that he would be pleased with them.

7.22.2.en: The reason for the divine wrath against the people is their worship of idols and their offering the dearest thing they have, their sons and their daughters, as burnt offerings to please the gods, and this is what God did not command, for He is a tender God who asks for the care of children and compassion toward them.

7.23.0.en: God declares what will happen when the army of Babylon attacks and kills many of the Jews, so that the valley of Hinnom near Jerusalem is filled with their corpses, and not the corpses of animals. It is a symbol of the eternal torment that they will meet in Gehenna by their refusal to repent.

7.24.0.en: Because of the multitude of the corpses of the Jews, birds of prey come and eat from them and no one drives them away, and this is an expression of the total ruin, and of the appalling nature of the Babylonian attack as a discipline for the stubborn people.

7.25.0.en: After the demolition of the temple and the destruction of Jerusalem and the killing of the Jews in it, and indeed in the cities of Judah around it, grief casts its shadow over the hearts of those who remain, and their joys and feasts cease, whether personal ones, such as rejoicing in new marriages, or public feasts, because the ruin has become total.

7.25.1.en: Humiliation and ruin for the people's rejection of God (1) The humiliation of the Jews (vv. 1-3)

7.25.2.en: 1- At that time, saith the LORD, they shall bring out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of his princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of their graves: 2- And they shall spread them before the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served, and after whom they have walked, and whom they have sought, and whom they have worshipped: they shall not be gathered, nor be buried; they shall be for dung upon the face of the earth. 3- And death shall be chosen rather than life by all the residue of them that remain of this evil family, which remain in all the places whither I have driven them, saith the LORD of hosts.

8.0.s.en: (5) Rejected His house and His people

8.0.0.en: At that time: the time of Babylon's attack on the kingdom of Judah.

8.0.1.en: So that Jeremiah may alert his people to repent and turn back from the worship of idols, such as the worship of the sun and the heavens, he declares to them that when the armies of Babylon attack them they will dig up the graves of their fathers and bring out their bones and throw them everywhere before what they call gods, such as the sun and the heavens, which will not profit them at all. God will allow this humiliation because they did not obey Him, and perhaps they will repent, and this will be done to the graves of the great ones of the Jews, the prophets and leaders and kings and priests, as a degradation of the Jews.

8.1.0.en: Dung: manure, that is, the droppings of cattle.

8.1.1.en: When the Babylonians bring out the bones of the dead they are before the sun and the moon and the heavens which they worshiped and which did not profit them at all, and their bones become despised, like the manure of animals thrown on the ground.

8.1.2.en: When God allows you to be despised by others, review yourself, perhaps He is calling you to repent and hold fast to Him, so that He delivers you from their hands and your relationship with Him increases. So do not fear what they say, and do not be distressed by their contempt, for it is worthless, and God will honor you in the heavens above all.

8.2.0.en: The remnant of the Jews will wish for death, after many of them have died from the abundance of distress, to be rid of the humiliation in which they have come to be, and this is because of their lack of attachment to God, to whom they ought to have returned, and He would have received them and delivered them.

8.2.2.en: 4- Moreover thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the LORD; Shall they fall, and not arise? shall he turn away, and not return?

8.2.3.en: 5- Why then is this people of Jerusalem slidden back by a perpetual backsliding? they hold fast deceit, they refuse to return. 6- I hearkened and heard, but they spake not aright: no man repented him of his wickedness, saying, What have I done? every one turned to his course, as the horse rusheth into the battle. 7- Yea, the stork in the heaven knoweth her appointed times; and the turtle and the crane and the swallow observe the time of their coming; but my people know not the judgment of the LORD. 8- How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain. 9- The wise men are ashamed, they are dismayed and taken: lo, they have rejected the word of the LORD; and what wisdom is in them? 10- Therefore will I give their wives unto others, and their fields to them that shall inherit them: for every one from the least even unto the greatest is given to covetousness, from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. 11- For they have healed the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace. 12- Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore shall they fall among them that fall: in the time of their visitation they shall be cast down, saith the LORD.

8.3.0.en: God rebukes His people with a fact, which is that whoever falls on the way, or in anything wrong, must go back and return to what is right, and this is the logical course of action. Why then do they persist in their sins and remain firm in evil, relying on the cunning and deceptive words of the false prophets?

8.4.1.en: He compares their persistence in evil to a horse advancing in battle that does not want to turn back from its way, for this is the order of war: striving to the end, even to death; so they too advanced in evil, insisting on it until death, and do not want to return and repent.

8.4.2.en: Be attentive to the voice of God that calls you to review your thoughts and your words and your behavior, even if you are accustomed to them, that is, many years have passed over them. Seek God with humility, and submit to your father of confession, and do not be angry with the one who punishes you, or neglect his word.

8.5.0.en: The stork: a large bird with a beak, and long legs and a long red neck; it is one of the birds of prey, that is, those that swoop on their prey.

8.5.1.en: The swallow: a small bird with long wings and swift flight, one of the tame birds, and its voice is beautiful.

8.5.2.en: God directs the attention of His people to the fact that animals such as birds return from their flight at a fixed time to which they are accustomed, but the sons of His people do not want to return from their sins although they are the best of creatures and the wisest of them, so it would be natural for them to return to their sound position, which is life with God.

8.6.0.en: He affirms to them their insistence on deceiving themselves with the words of the false scribes, thinking that they are wise because they possess the Holy Bible, and because of the presence of the temple in their city Jerusalem, but all this is not enough if they do not repent.

8.7.0.en: He shows the sad end of those who think themselves wise, that is, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, when the army of Babylon attacks and takes them captive, and this is the natural result for whoever refuses to obey the word of God and to repent.

8.8.1.en: God shows a basic reason for their not repenting, which is their attachment to money and material things, and the whole people fell into this sin, even their leaders, such as the priests and the false prophets, and the result is their falling under the Babylonian attack and the taking from them of their wives and fields, that is, their being stripped of all the material things and lusts for which they lived; all this that perhaps in the end they will return to God.

8.9.1.en: One of the reasons for their not repenting is their not treating their sins, but holding fast to the evil within them and believing the words of the false prophets that they have peace and God is pleased with them, although their sins have corrupted them, and they need to be healed from them by repentance.

8.10.1.en: They persisted in evil and base lusts shamelessly, and were not ashamed of their cheap deeds, so it was necessary to punish them with captivity.

8.10.3.en: 13- I will surely consume them, saith the LORD: there shall be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade; and the things that I have given them shall pass away from them. 14- Why do we sit still? assemble yourselves, and let us enter into the defenced cities, and let us be silent there: for the LORD our God hath put us to silence, and given us water of gall to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD. 15- We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of health, and behold trouble! 16- The snorting of his horses was heard from Dan: the whole land trembled at the sound of the neighing of his strong ones; for they are come, and have devoured the land, and all that is in it; the city, and those that dwell therein. 17- For, behold, I will send serpents, cockatrices, among you, which will not be charmed, and they shall bite you, saith the LORD.

8.11.0.en: The vine: the grapevine, that is, the tree of the grape.

8.11.1.en: Because of the multitude of the sins of His people, God decided to drive them out of their land and kill them at the hand of the Babylonians, as the grapes are gathered from the vine and the fruits of the fig from its tree, and His gifts to them are taken from them, and this is because they did not gather around God and worship Him, but worshiped idols and walked in their evil lusts.

8.12.0.en: Gall: bitter, and it is often the colocynth plant.

8.12.1.en: The Jews were afraid when they heard of the attack of the armies of Babylon, so they hurried to their fortified cities to take refuge in them, and sat in fear and silence, and they had no strength to fight the enemies and defend themselves, but in despair they fell silent awaiting death, and God left them in despair and silence because they did not seek Him.

8.13.0.en: The Jews expected peace and healing to come to them from their hard distress, as their prophets deceived them, but sadly they found war instead of peace, and instead of healing, ruin and calamities and killing, because they relied on the lie of their prophets and refused to obey God through the mouth of Jeremiah.

8.14.0.en: Snorting or neighing: the sounds of horses.

8.14.1.en: Dan lies north of Jerusalem, and from there the armies of Babylon attacked with their armed horsemen and the strong sounds of the horses, and destroyed Jerusalem and Judea.

8.15.0.en: Which will not be charmed: the one who specializes in gathering snakes cannot gather them by using the charm, that is, the works of demons.

8.15.1.en: Cockatrices: a very poisonous kind of snake.

8.15.2.en: God makes clear the strength of the Babylonians, which the Jews cannot resist, and compares it to snakes that bite them with their venom, and it is impossible to resist or repel these snakes by any of the ways of the sorcerers who gather snakes.

8.15.3.en: When you hear the threats of God against the wicked, hasten to repentance and you will save your soul and regain your peace whatever afflictions surround you, and trust in the tenderness of God who seeks your salvation by gentleness or by warning. (4) The prophet's grief (vv. 18-22)

8.15.4.en: 18- When I would comfort myself against sorrow, my heart is faint in me. 19- Behold the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people because of them that dwell in a far country: Is not the LORD in Zion? is not her king in her? Why have they provoked me to anger with their graven images, and with strange vanities?

8.15.5.en: 20- The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved. 21- For the hurt of the daughter of my people am I hurt; I am black; astonishment hath taken hold on me. 22- Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?

8.16.1.en: When the prophet saw all the ruin that would come upon the kingdom of Judah, he was very grieved and his heart was pained, and he expressed that by declaring his need for someone to lift from him this grief for the destruction of his people.

8.17.0.en: Their graven images: statues of the pagan gods.

8.17.1.en: The prophet expresses the sufferings of his people who will be taken captive to far countries and cry out from the humiliation of slavery, and he asks: where is God, the King of the Jews, who protects them? Why did He leave them to captivity and humiliation? .. And God answers him, I left them because they left Me by their worship of idols.

8.18.0.en: The farmer waits for the time of harvest, which is the months of April and May, to rejoice in gathering his crops.

8.18.1.en: And here he expresses the waiting of the people of God for Him to deliver them from the Babylonians; the months of harvest passed and the Babylonian devastation of the kingdom of Judah was still continuing, so the people said to themselves, perhaps He will deliver us in the summer at the gathering of the summer crops in the months of July and August, but sadly God did not deliver them, because they did not repent of their sins, so all this ruin came upon them.

8.19.0.en: The prophet returns and expresses the sorrows of his heart as a father of this people, as he sees their humiliation and suffers and grieves within, and even marvels at the total ruin that came upon them and upon the temple of God, although he knows that all this is because of their evils, but he cannot stop his feelings as a human being, and his suffering for them.

8.20.0.en: Balm: a tree more than four meters high that gives a fragrant scent, and if its stem is struck with a sharp tool a sticky liquid like milk comes out of it, which quickly hardens, and it is used as an ointment for the treatment of diseases, and it was costly; it is what is called the balsam plant.

8.20.1.en: Gilead: a region located east of the river Jordan and extending to the land of the Arabs.

8.20.2.en: When the prophet sees many wounded among his people and severe humiliation, he cries out asking for medicine and a physician to rescue them, and gives an example of medicines, the balsam plant, famous for the treatment of many diseases, so that it heals the wounds of many and then their wounds are bound up until they heal. By the physician and the medicine he means not only material medicine but rather spiritual medicine, that is, he appeals to God to lead His people to repentance and forgive them and lift His wrath from them.

8.20.3.en: May you feel for those far from God and for the suffering and pray for them, and seek to bring them back to the Church so that they find rest from their sins and troubles, knowing that your prayer profits them greatly and God rejoices in them. Lying and idol worship are the cause of Jerusalem's destruction
